title: Old-Time Root Cellar Airing
subtitle: 1917 USDA Wisdom
items: Wet the floor if air is dry
intro: Old USDA storage bulletins said a root cellar lives or dies by its air. Here is how farm families kept theirs cold, damp and fresh all winter, rewritten for today.
desc: Old-time root cellar tips inspired by USDA Farmers' Bulletin 879, Home Storage of Vegetables (1917): use a thermometer, open vents on cold nights and close them on warm days, keep the cellar near 32–40°F, add moisture when the air is dry and keep apples apart from potatoes and turnips. Full list on the blog.

title: Start a Winter Compost Pile
subtitle: Free Soil for Spring
intro: Fall leaves and kitchen scraps are free fertilizer. Start a pile now and it will be breaking down into dark garden soil by planting time.
desc: How to start a compost pile in late fall for beginner vegetable gardeners: shred fallen leaves, mix roughly 2–3 parts browns to 1 part greens, add kitchen scraps, keep it as damp as a wrung-out sponge and build it about 3 feet square so it holds heat. Full list on the blog.

title: Indoor Seed Starting Checklist
subtitle: Get Ready for Spring
items: A small fan for sturdy stems
desc: Indoor seed starting checklist for beginners: seed trays with drainage holes, fresh sterile seed-starting mix, a grow light kept a few inches above seedlings, plant labels, and a small fan for sturdy stems. Most vegetables are started 6–8 weeks before the last frost. (Contains affiliate links.)

title: How to Can Apple Pie Filling
subtitle: USDA Water Bath Method
intro: Home-canned apple pie filling means a pie is only a crust away all winter. These are the key safety points from the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning.
desc: How to can apple pie filling the USDA way: thicken with ClearJel (not flour or cornstarch), blanch apple slices for 1 minute, fill hot jars leaving 1-inch headspace and process pints or quarts 25 minutes in a boiling water bath at 0–1,000 ft, adding time at higher altitudes. Full list on the blog.

title: How to Dry Mushrooms
subtitle: Easy Winter Pantry Staple
items: Dry at low heat until crisp
Soak in hot water to use
intro: Dried mushrooms take up almost no space and add deep flavor to winter soups and stews. Use store-bought or cultivated mushrooms only.
desc: How to dry mushrooms at home for the winter pantry: brush them clean instead of soaking, slice evenly, dry at low heat until the pieces are brittle and snap, cool, then store airtight in a dark cupboard. Rehydrate in hot water for soups and stews. Full list on the blog.

title: Use a Generator Safely
subtitle: Winter Power Outage Prep
intro: A generator keeps the freezer and furnace fan running in a winter outage, but carbon monoxide is deadly and invisible. Follow these rules every time.
desc: Portable generator safety for a winter power outage: run it outdoors only, at least 20 feet from doors and windows, never in a garage, keep battery CO alarms inside, let it cool before refueling and use heavy outdoor-rated cords or a transfer switch. Full list on the blog.
